tags.gist: Supports Sections V and VI but asks that sponsors report a reproducibility floor, the device's variation on identical inputs, treating smaller differences as uninformative.
Cites a study where a clinical agent's action changed in 8.7 percent of identical re-runs, varying eightfold across actions, with no disparity finding.
Says the right null is the device's difference against itself; report floors per graded endpoint under the marketed configuration, not pooled.
Wants any benchmark gating a decision to carry a documented floor, noting saturation arrives when device spread falls below benchmark noise.
Would have sponsors state the minimum detectable difference, since a null subgroup result without it carries no information.
Says the floor should set monitoring's minimum detectable effect, driving sampling volume and thresholds, and be re-established after model changes.
Citing judge-model instability, says supervisors cannot detect changes below their own instability, their prompts need change control, and shared-model errors correlate.
Wants acceptance criteria set per action, measuring highest-consequence actions most carefully, since instability varied eightfold across actions.
Proposes no numeric instability threshold, leaving that to the Section IV framework, asking only that the quantity be measured and reported.
Asks CDRH to add to Sections V and VI a reported reproducibility floor, because every evaluation compares differences and generative variation is not zero.
Details the study: 8.7 percent action instability across 4,320 cells, uneven by action, replicated on a second model, only partly reduced by voting.
Wants a per-endpoint reproducibility floor as the null, with overlapping intervals read as lacking resolution; acknowledges the bounded extra cost.
Says gating benchmarks need a documented floor so reviewers see what differences they can resolve, and noise-based saturation precedes ceiling effects.
Wants submissions reporting no subgroup difference to state the minimum detectable difference, since underpowered audits do not show fairness.
Wants degradation triggers and cadence justified by the floor, showing what drift they could catch, with the floor re-measured after model changes.
Applies the floor to supervisors: no credit below their instability, supervisory prompts under change control, no assumed independence from a shared model.
Wants per-action floors and acceptance criteria along the trajectory, since aggregates favour frequent over consequential decisions and steps compound.
Sets no instability threshold and does not call devices unstable; wants the number reported so the two-axis framework can guide the call.
